The haze takes Old Kohler on his way home with his new-year ham: burning face, blocked throat, the memory of a drunk's words about straw falling when the wind blows — the unsmoked cigarette in his fingers, and one last unspoken question. 'Why?'

Across East Borough, the docks and the factory district the old fall like felled trees and their neighbours after them — on the Tuesday of the last week of 1349, Backlund is shrouded in haze
